_about: Orchestrator Turn 6 judgement data (attempt-02, public-evidence variant). Groups are ordered in the native judge order: constructor/initialize -> setters -> deposit -> accrue -> borrow -> liquidate -> withdraw -> cross-chain receive (mapped: createRaffle -> (no setters) -> buyEntries -> requestDraw/_settleWinningTicket -> (no borrow) -> enableRefunds forced exit -> redeem/release/_update -> fulfillRandomWords async callback). Gates: G1 code path stops it? G2 preconditions reachable? G3 harm to someone other than the attacker? G4 real value? UNCERTAIN counts as ALLOWS. Gates are evaluated for every group; for LEAD groups they drive promotion/demotion.

mechanisms.summary: A hostile prize contract can call Raffle.onERC721Received itself during its own safeTransferFrom (F:128) and answer the factory ownerOf/status checks (F:129-134), producing an Active raffle with nothing escrowed; the same contract answers the delivery checks (Raffle.sol:335, :405).

mitigations.quote: The recommendation is to document the prize trust boundary for buyers, not to change code.

F:129/F:132 and Raffle.sol:421-426 verify escrow only through calls and answers of the prize contract itself, so a hostile prize can forge onERC721Received and ownerOf.
G2: ALLOWS

G3: Buyers of that raffle are not the sponsor, but they opted into an unvetted prize contract; the harm equals entering a raffle for a worthless prize.
G4: BLOCKS
No incremental loss is established beyond the buyer-visible worthless-prize risk, and no check that only queries the prize contract can remove it.

mechanisms.summary: After the reserve is met, the sponsor buys entries from a fresh address in the last block before endTime. NftWon pays 95% of the gross pot, including those entries, back to sponsorRecipient (Raffle.sol:544, :554), so each sponsor entry costs 5% net but carries full weight in the draw (Raffle.sol:518). Earlier buyers cannot exit: refunds open only at endTime+2d (:286-287), and the draw opens at endTime (:242).

mitigations.quote: Stop the sale at the reserve in buyEntries (`if (lastEntry > reserveEntries) revert ...`), so no sponsor-rebated entries can be minted after organic demand meets the reserve.

cautions.quote: A sponsor fill of the gap below the reserve remains possible; it is tracked as a separate lead.

G1: ALLOWS

buyEntries (:215-221) checks only status, sale time, recipient, count and overflow; it has no cap once the reserve is met and no exclusion of sponsor-controlled buyers. _update (:497-502) screens only protocol plumbing.
G2: ALLOWS

Sponsor capital is locked only from endTime-1 until settle plus release (minutes to hours), and 95% comes back in NftWon. It is not flash-loanable, but the attack pays whenever NFT value > 5% of the final pot; sybil purchases cannot be told apart from real ones.
G3: Victims are the organic ticket holders who bought before the sale closed: their odds of winning the NFT are diluted while their USDC goes to sponsorRecipient and the treasury.
G4: ALLOWS
Expected value moves between cohorts. R07 example: Alice -9,000 USDC EV, sponsor +4,500, treasury +4,500.

groups.severity_reason: The loss is a probabilistic transfer of expected value between cohorts with no insolvency. I was torn with High because the sponsor creates every precondition, and chose the lower.

chains.summary: The sponsor tops up the reserve shortfall for about 5% of its cost to force NftWon (L-2/L-3), then blocks delivery of a sponsor-administered prize (M-1). It collects 95% of the buyers' pot while the winner receives nothing. Combined, this is worse than either alone: M-1 alone needs organic demand >= reserve, and the flip alone still leaves buyers a chance at the NFT. It is not reported as a separate finding because one untrusted actor (the sponsor) controls both legs, and the only trust boundary crossed is M-1's prize-contract boundary.
